title: API request amplification investigation and graceful fastpath hotpatch
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
A high-severity customer escalation reported a sustained spike in server errors (500/502/504) and long-tail timeouts on Hosted API endpoints during a tenant migration. Early traces show amplified requests originating from a mix of client-side retry bursts and edge proxy path duplication. The burst caused KV cache thrashing on serving hosts, increased contention for model worker slots, and a cascade of queueing timeouts and 5xx responses.

Scope & Impact:
- Affected multiple large tenants during their heavy upload/ingestion windows (not all tenants).
- Elevated P99 latency from ~450ms to >2.5s and error rate jumped to 6-8% for some routes.
- Incidents surfaced via support escalations and automated SLO alerts.

Repro steps / diagnostics performed so far:
1) Correlated burst windows with tenant burst timestamp from customer support logs and per-tenant traces.
2) Captured edge request traces showing duplicated request IDs and missing idempotency headers on some SDK flows.
3) Observed concurrent inflight requests per tenant exceed configured soft limits; KV cache eviction rate spiked during the bursts.
4) Flamegraphs from model workers show increased time in KV cache lookup and cache-miss handling.
5) Temporary per-tenant throttles applied reduced error rate but impacted throughput.

Root cause hypothesis:
A confluence of: (A) client-side retries (without idempotency keys) + edge proxy retransmit behavior during connection churn; (B) lack of request-level deduplication at the edge; (C) KV cache pressure on serving hosts causing increased model worker latency; (D) global retry amplification from SDKs and downstream proxies creating feedback loops.

Proposed immediate fix (hotpatch):
- Implement an edge-side graceful fastpath that deduplicates requests for a short window (200ms) based on idempotency-key or a best-effort composite key (client-ip + route + recent-nonce).
- Add a conservative per-tenant inflight limiter to enforce fairness and avoid single-tenant saturation (soft limit + token-bucket with burst allowance).
- Short-circuit heavy synchronous calls to fallback variant model (small quantized model) when worker queue depth exceeds threshold (configurable per-route).
- Temporarily update SDK guidance (and send customer communication) to attach idempotency-key on retriable calls; recommend backoff tuning.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary deploy fastpath to a small set of edge nodes and 5% traffic using tenant bucketing for one hour, monitor errors/latency.
2) If stable, widen to 25% and validate across peak windows; then to 100%.
3) Simultaneously enable per-tenant limiter as feature flag that can be tuned.

Monitoring & success criteria:
- Reduce error rate on affected routes to <=0.5% (baseline) and P99 latency to <600ms within 30m of rollout.
- Dashboard: hosted-api/edge/deduplication, hosted-api/worker/queue-depth, per-tenant error-rate. (See dashboard link in comments.)

Risk & rollback plan:
- Deduplication may incorrectly coalesce non-idempotent requests: we will only apply for routes marked idempotent in routing config and fall back to conservative composite-key dedupe for unmarked routes in canary.
- Rollback by disabling fastpath and per-tenant limiter feature flags; immediate revert PR ready.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem to capture root cause and long-term solution (persistent request fingerprinting + stronger SDK idempotency), include SDK changes and docs.
